newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Three more Russian firms say near Iraqi oil deals.
newsitem.headline: Three more Russian firms say near Iraqi oil deals.

text.p: Three more Russian oil companies are close to completing deals with Baghdad for what could amount to 1.15 million tonnes of Iraqi crude oil over six months, company officials said on Thursday.
Rosneft spokesman Vladimir Tumarkin said a delegation from the state oil holding firm would fly to Baghdad on Thursday to sign a contract for 400,000 tonnes of Iraqi crude over six months.
Russia's Alfa-Eko trading house said it was close to completing a contract to buy around 350,000 tonnes of oil with an option to increase the amount later.
Alfa-Eko spokesman Andrei Suntsov said that the amount had not yet been fixed and could change.
But he said Baghdad was seeking to award Russian companies contracts for 25 to 30 percent of the total amount of oil Iraq will export under its deal with the United Nations.
Iraq is expected to export around 600,000 barrels per day.
Sergei Tumanov, head of Tekhnoneft, a unit of Mashinoimport, said negotiations were underway for the unit to buy 400,000 tonnes over six months.
He said the contract would be finalised hopefully by the end of the year and definitely in the first 10 days of January 1997.
Three Russian companies -- Zarubezhneft, NK LUKoil and Nafta-Moskva -- have already signed contracts with Iraq to buy 1.3 million tonnes of crude oil and are awaiting U.N. approval.
The new contracts, if signed in the volumes indicated, would bring Russia's share to 2.45 million tonnes over six months.

Iraq began exporting oil for the first time in six years on December 16 from the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan under a U.N. deal in which Baghdad is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of crude over six months for food and medicine.
